title: Reinforcement learning based automated anesthesia system for gastrointestinal endoscopy with a multicenter randomized trial.
summary: In a multicenter randomized trial of 418 adults undergoing endoscopy, AAS-GE and clinician-managed anesthesia had similar observed hypoxemia rates (14.42% vs 14.29%; OR 1.01, 95% CI 0.59–1.75; P=.968). Induction was shorter, while body movement was more frequent with AAS-GE. The published protocol powered a test of a difference based on expected rates of 20% versus 10%; it did not specify a noninferiority margin, so the trial does not establish that a prespecified noninferiority criterion was met.
ai_technology: Offline RL learned the dose-control policy; the model was selected and refined before the randomized evaluation

evidence.tested: The primary report gives hypoxemia rates of 14.42% vs 14.29% (OR 1.01, 95% CI 0.59–1.75; P=.968), shorter induction, and more body movement with AAS-GE. The published protocol's sample-size calculation tests a difference assuming expected rates of 20% vs 10%; no noninferiority margin is specified.
evidence.unknown: A prespecified noninferiority margin and corresponding noninferiority analysis were not identified in the published protocol or primary report; the observed nonsignificant difference does not itself establish noninferiority.
evidence.ai_role: Offline RL learned the dose-control policy; the model was selected and refined before the randomized evaluation.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
